mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate below 0.1% compresses the risk-free rate, reducing the discount rate for equity cash flows and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as monetary policy remains accommodative.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.1%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 6.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that precede corporate earnings contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE > 6.0, or the Rank IC over the last 2 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate broad-based consumer demand contraction, which typically triggers negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced corporate revenue visibility.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or the interaction term (HOUST × RSAFS) has a Rank IC below 0.04 over the last 3 years.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO < 105) signals manufacturing slowdowns that reduce corporate profit growth potential, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days during economic deceleration.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when INDPRO < 105, or the Rank IC for INDPRO decline is below 0.03 over the last 3 years.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained employment growth above 140,000 thousand persons (PAYEMS > 140000) supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as labor market strength translates to economic momentum.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when PAYEMS > 140000, or the Rank IC over the last 2 years is below 0.04.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL index level above 260 indicates elevated inflation pressures that typically trigger monetary policy tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real rates rise.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 260, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and rising inflation (CPIAUCSL > 260) indicate demand destruction amid inflationary pressures, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to earnings uncertainty.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when HOUST declines and CPIAUCSL > 260, or the interaction term (HOUST × CPIAUCSL) has a Rank IC below 0.04 over the last 3 years.

mechanism_narrative: Monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 1.0%) increase borrowing costs and reduce corporate leverage, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as equity valuations face pressure.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 1.0%, or the Rank IC for the FEDFUNDS > 1.0% signal is below 0.03 over the last 3 years.
